notes.q: What is the independently verified Q3 casualty distribution?
notes.ans: Not independently verified. One originator holds a quarterly count.
body: The UN (BINUH Human Rights Service) records at least 1,167 people killed and 459 injured between 1 July and 30 September 2026: 45% during gang attacks; 50% during operations by national security forces, including extrajudicial executions involving police officers, actions by a private military company, and GSF patrols; and 5% during violence by self-defense groups and unorganized members of the population (“Bwa Kalé”).
By place, the report gives 85% for the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area in its text and 85% for the West Department on its map, then 12% Artibonite, 2% Grand Nord, 1% Centre. See D-509-05.

S/2026/800 counts 1,123 killed and 440 injured between 15 July and 12 October 2026, 52% of them during security operations. It is the same originator, and its period is different: it is neither combined with the quarterly figure nor counted as corroboration.

Independent counts exist for one event only. For the attack on Kenscoff on the night of 23–24 August, the mayor of Kenscoff told AFP about 40 were killed; the UN counts at least 47 killed and 52 kidnapped; RNDDH counts at least 164 killed and more than 70 kidnapped across the July, late-August and mid-September attacks. The scopes differ; see D-509-09.

notes.q: What operational support and strength are independently established for GSF?
notes.ans: Neither is independently established. Each figure rests on one originator.
body: Strength: 1,083 military and 16 civilian personnel on 8 July 2026 (UN).
About 1,500 troops deployed, according to the United States ambassador to the UN, 29 September 2026. One originator, relayed by two outlets.
On 1 September the GSF spokesperson said the force would not reach 5,500 by October and declined to give the number deployed, citing operational reasons.

Operations: starting in September, the GSF supported at least six operations by HNP specialised units (Croix-des-Bouquets, Kenscoff, Port-au-Prince and Tabarre; Dessalines), continued patrols in Cité Soleil and Tabarre, and conducted at least two independent operations (Port-au-Prince, Gros-Morne). Nine gang members were killed and two injured; about 20 people were arrested.
The Human Rights Service monitored seven GSF operations during the quarter. See D-509-07.
804 GSF personnel (767 men, 37 women) attended human-rights sessions. This is a training count, not a strength figure.
Between 6 March and 31 July 2026 the force did not take part in operations against gangs in La Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil.

notes.q: Does a written instrument place any parallel contingent under GSF command?
notes.ans: Candidate: no. The parallel force on record answers to the Prime Minister's Office.
body: BINUH describes a government-established “task force” of police officers and personnel from a foreign private military company conducting ground and explosive-drone operations, and cites no instrument governing it.

Human Rights Watch records that the task force was created on 1 March 2025 by the Prime Minister and the Transitional Presidential Council, is coordinated by the Prime Minister's Office according to BINUH, operates with support from Vectus Global, and that its command structure has not been made public.

Two originators, one dated in the quarter, describe the force outside the GSF line of command. No written instrument places it under GSF command. The desk has not declared confidence; the judgment is unsigned.
El Salvador's transitional law (29 September, in force 2 October) concerns participation in the GSF, not a parallel contingent.

notes.q: What is the end-state status of any parallel contingent?
notes.ans: No published end-state for any parallel contingent is held.
body: BINUH states no end-state, term or mandate for the private military company personnel in the government task force.
Vectus Global's owner has said the company signed a one-year contract with the transitional government. One originator, before the period; the contract text is not public.
El Salvador’s law sets a 12-month term from 2 October 2026 for participation in the GSF. It is not an end-state for a parallel contingent and is not counted here.

notes.q: What movement is independently established across three election indicators?
notes.ans: None. No reading of the three indicators exists for the quarter.
body: The indicator definitions (Cadre 7, v1) date from 03.11.2026, after the period, and remain a draft until the first signed Cadre 7 reading. There is no baseline and no reading.

The electoral calendar itself is dual-sourced for the quarter: published by the CEP on 27 July (first round 13.12.2026, runoff 21.02.2027), reported by The Haitian Times, AFP and CMC. It was superseded on 28.10.2026.

Context, not indicator values: BINUH documents gang interference in the electoral process. The Brooklyn gang leader reportedly drew up a list of candidates for Cité Soleil, and on 29 July shot dead two residents for denouncing it. On the night of 23–24 September former deputy Dupner Clément was found dead in Baradères; no link to his political activities was established. In a statement dated 1 September, the leader of the 400 Mawozo gang proclaimed himself “mayor of Croix-des-Bouquets”.

notes.q: How many PNH-related files reached a judge or custody record?
notes.ans: No record. No source held gives this number.
body: The HRS documented 44 cases of extrajudicial executions and attempted extrajudicial executions involving HNP personnel (37 deaths, 7 injuries). They will be referred to the General Inspectorate (IGPNH) in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Of 279 cases (308 victims) referred to the IGPNH in 2025 and 2026, 257 remain under investigation and 22 have been finalised but await closure reports. The IGPNH is the police inspectorate, not a judge; none of these figures is counted here.
The HRS has received no information that the authorities opened investigations into deaths and injuries caused during security force operations.

Custody: a transfer agreement for people apprehended during operations was signed on 14 July 2026. Its text is not public and it counts no one. The disposition of the roughly 20 people arrested in GSF operations is not reported.
RNDDH's report on the Kenscoff attacks criticises police passivity and the withdrawal of units; as relayed, it mentions no judicial proceedings.

notes.q: Which political authority instruments were legally in force during Q3 2026?
notes.ans: Candidate: partly listed. One instrument meets the two-originator test.
body: Electoral decree. The government published a decree on 2 June 2026; amendments agreed with the CEP and political parties were published in Le Moniteur on 2 July 2026, without republishing the full text. Two originators; dated in the quarter.
Electoral budget. The Prime Minister's Office and the CEP announced agreement on a US$120 million budget on 3 July; on 28 July it had not yet been approved by the Cabinet or published.

Carried, dated before the period: the Transitional Presidential Council's mandate ended on 7 February 2026 with no successor council; authority sits with an unelected prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, without a president or parliament. Two originators, both 02.2026; not re-read for the quarter.

International instruments: Resolution 2793 (30.09.2025) authorised the GSF; Resolution 2829 renewed it on 29.09.2026 to 31.03.2027; Resolution 2814 extends BINUH to 31.01.2027; the UN sanctions regime runs to October 2027.
Not yet in force: the new Criminal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure (decree of March 2020, revised June 2025), expected early 2027.
Whether international mandates count as political-authority instruments is left to the desk.

movement_rule: Against the previous signed month: improved or deteriorated when at least two indicators move the same way (±1 road segment, ±2 percentage points, ±2 % of centres) and none moves against them; otherwise unchanged.

chronology.e: Amendments to the electoral decree of 2 June are published in Le Moniteur, agreed by the CEP, the government and political parties.
The Prime Minister's Office and the CEP announce agreement on a US$120 million electoral budget.
The CEP publishes the electoral calendar: first round 13 December 2026, runoff and local elections 21 February 2027. Superseded 28.10.2026.
Gangs attack Kenscoff overnight, including a church sheltering displaced people. Counts differ: about 40 killed (mayor), at least 47 killed and 52 kidnapped (UN).
The Security Council adopts Resolution 2829 by 12 votes to none, with China, Pakistan and Russia abstaining. The GSF mandate now runs to 31 March 2027.

method: A republication of the same report is not corroboration; one originator through two channels counts once.
Candidate: a cell that meets the originator test but has no declared confidence. It is shown, unsigned, until the desk signs or strikes it.
Confidence declared before claim; never raised after.
Sources graded A (official or primary), B (established press or monitor), C (not yet graded: listed, never counted).
Every judgment marked signed or unsigned.
Empty is a result. An empty cell is never filled by inference.
No policy recommendations. No targeting lists. No operational advice.
One question per note. Objects over narrative.
cell_order_note: Candidate: two independent originators, one dated in the quarter; awaiting the desk's confidence and signature.
revisions: Title: “Elite Intel Report” replaced by “Quarterly Record”. Subtitle shortened to “Security allocation and parallel force”.
Section names: Objects → Notes; Held, not listed → Single-source events; “What would fill this cell” → “What would complete this cell”.

New status, Candidate: originator test met, confidence and signature left to the desk. Two cells move from empty to candidate: 03 Written command clarity (Parallel) and 07 Political authority instruments (Partly listed).
Twelve sources added (S21–S32) from a search on 16.11.2026; every one is linked, dated and graded.
Chronology: three new dual-sourced entries (02.07, 03.07, 23–24.08); the 13 December entry is re-dated to 27.07, its event date. The v1.0 date is struck in E-509.
Election calendar rebuilt: 13 dated items with originator counts, including the 02.07 decree, the 03.07 budget, the start of registration and candidate registration.
Two discrepancies added (D-509-09 Kenscoff toll; D-509-10 start of registration). D-509-02 now notes three outside sources dating the attack 23–24 August.
GSF plate: the spokesperson's refusal to publish a figure (01.09) is shown as a recorded absence.
Mark: the Legba vèvè (keeper of the gate) replaces the borrowed Cadre 7 line mark. It is poured on load and used as the seal.

Interface: board filter, reading progress, section index that follows the reader, reveal on scroll, originator meters that fill in view, expand or collapse all notes, highlighted source on arrival, print button. All static under reduced motion and without JavaScript.
PDF: same record, A4, running header now reads “Quarterly Record”.

v1.2 — The vèvè is now poured, not drawn: grains of cornmeal fall from a moving hand, the upright of the crossroads first, then the crossbar, each from the centre outward. The crisp mark settles over the grains and stands in candlelight. “Trace again” repeats it; any tap or key finishes it.

v1.2 — A rail of eight signs on the left edge finds the sections: crossroads (Board), cane (Holders), leaf (Notes), lattice (Registers), volute (Chronology), gate (Method), star (Sources), eye (Revisions). The same sign heads each section and its entry in the top index. Keys 1–8 jump to a section.
v1.2 — Interface: the rail shows reading progress; the top index keeps the current section in view on small screens; section headings draw in. No record content changed.

v1.3 — New section 02, Plates: an evidence matrix (which originator supports which cell, counted or only held), the quarter on one line (dual-sourced against single-source events), a map of the places the record names over BINUH's casualty shares, and BINUH's second- and third-quarter counts side by side.
v1.3 — Sections renumbered 01–09; a ninth sign (compass) for Plates. Every plate is drawn from the record, carries its originator count, and adds no figure the record does not hold.

v1.4 — New mark, supplied by the desk: 777, a radiant circle holding a triangle and an inner circle between two crossed rings, 509. It replaces the Legba vèvè on the cover, in the header and as the seal. On load it burns: each line catches from the centre, flares, cools through orange and red, and is left as ash, with sparks lifting off; afterwards it smoulders. “Burn again” repeats it; any tap or key finishes it. The same mark and burn sit on the Cadre 509 door of the hub. No record content changed.
